evidence.V1: Three-quarter reads as a roof slope with an eave board, but the front view reads as a flat brick wall and the silhouette is just a tilted slab with tiny course notches.
evidence.V2: Big slab and medium shingle courses plus a timber eave/gable trim, but no small-scale detail (no ridge nails, cracked or slipped slates) and shingles are near-uniform long rectangles.
evidence.V3: Shingles are long, thin, brick-like rectangles with very little overlap step, so the piece reads stiff and wall-like rather than a confident stylised roof with chunky lapped slates.
evidence.V4: Shingle edges and the timber eave/gable boards carry consistent chamfers that catch light in the eave and gable close-ups.
evidence.V5: Flat-light shingle close-up shows small notches/teeth at shingle corners where neighbouring chamfered shells intersect (228 cross-shell overlaps); minor but visible.
evidence.V6: Stone hue in 3 greys plus one timber brown secondary; brick and sandstone colourways keep the same 3-value plus trim structure.
evidence.V8: One LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + timber secondary, chamfers at kit scale - matches the modular spec.
evidence.V9: Studio line fits a walkable roof: Anchored, CollisionFidelity Default, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic; T1 tiling along X passes with IoU 1.0.

artifacts: small notch/tooth artifacts at shingle corners in the flat close-up where overlapping shingle shells intersect
top_fixes: Make the slates read as lapped roofing: shorter, chunkier slates with a clear step/shadow line per course and slight stagger/tilt, so it no longer reads as a brick wall
Clean the shingle-to-shingle intersections so no corner notches show in flat light
Add small detail (a few offset or chipped slates, ridge/eave nails) for the small tier
